narrative_events.details: Śaunaka asks Sūta what five empowered deities did. Sūta follows Mudgala’s answer to Dakṣa, recounting Pārvatī’s question to Śiva: she asks Gaṇeśa/devotee accounts after the five-deity boons, preferring them to wasted speech. Śiva joyfully embraces and answers her.

Śiva praises Pārvatī’s Gaṇeśa devotion, calls devotees Brahman-formed and liberating by sight, and says seekers/deity devotees omitting Gaṇeśa fail and fall to hell; the other gods likewise consign Gaṇeśa-disregarding or reviling devotees to hell. He calls Gaṇeśa everyone’s mother/father and first-worshipped Jyeṣṭharāja, requests constant Gaṇapatya company/dwelling in every direction, and praises Gaṇeśa/devotee accounts for worldly/otherworldly happiness, devotion and Brahman attainment by speaker/questioner/listener.

Gaṇeśa’s boons create five independent unbroken worlds: Śiva/Kailāsa, Viṣṇu/Vaikuṇṭha, Sun/Sauraloka, Śakti/Śaktiloka, Brahmā/Satyaloka. Initially mutual benefactors, they grow envious and claim unique supremacy. Viṣṇu creates body-water, sleeps; algae/creeper then earth develop. For play he creates a fragrant hundred-yojana navel-lotus. Visiting Brahmā wakes/honors him but accuses deluding creation and claims all depends on his own prior creation. Viṣṇu denies deceit, claims supreme preservation enables Brahmā and has no equal.

Brahmā invites Viṣṇu to inspect his belly. Viṣṇu enters by yogamāyā, sees cosmic creation including navel-lotus Viṣṇu, finds no end, exits and acknowledges Brahmā as guru/lord, then invites him inside. Brahmā enters by yoga, sees cosmic worlds and another Brahmā, finds no end. Viṣṇu closes exits by yogamāyā; Brahmā pierces a lotus-stalk doorway by yoga and exits angrily. Viṣṇu explains play/testing, asks pardon; Brahmā reciprocally apologizes for ignorant anger and acknowledges Viṣṇu’s greatness.

Brahmā/Viṣṇu regard themselves supreme and remember Śiva, Śakti and Sun to test them. Śiva comes first and, challenged, claims universal destruction and becomes a boundless luminous liṅga extending all directions. Brahmā proposes upward/downward searches. Before descent Viṣṇu asks a boon; Brahmā offers and Viṣṇu asks him to become his son. Brahmā acknowledges being caught by the offered promise and grants future yoga-created body from Viṣṇu’s navel lotus at creation. Both search Śiva’s limits in opposite directions, find none, return weary and hymn him.

The pair hymns Śaṅkara/Rudra/time/three-eyed, Umā lord, bull-mounted first deity, asking revealed nature for fearless worship. Śiva reveals Viṣṇu left, Brahmā right and full world in liṅga. They bow and ask withdrawal; he resumes former bull-bannered form, offers desired boons pleased by hymn, and promises reciters all wishes, his favor and his world at end.

Viṣṇu directs Brahmā to request Śiva as son so he becomes Viṣṇu’s grandson. Brahmā asks; Viṣṇu repeats; Śiva grants partial manifestation as Rudra from Brahmā’s forehead. Invited to inspect their powers with knowledge-sight, Śiva finds no end of either, calls the three supreme lords.

Sun comes at remembrance, shows boundless radiant animate/inanimate form; three lose radiance and physical sight, use knowledge-sight yet find no limit. He becomes gentle, views their powers likewise without end and calls them equal. Śakti arrives, shows gross/subtle complete-world form; four take refuge finding no end. Gentle Śakti views them and declares five equal. Under Gaṇeśa’s māyā they forget prior knowledge, ask how scripture’s one lord fits five, search above/below/ten directions without result, then meditate inwardly, attain unity and peace.

Gaṇarāja shows his form in their hearts: four arms, three eyes, trunk, one tusk, fan-ears, crooked trunk/great belly, red vermilion body, Śeṣa navel, crown/ornaments, Siddhi/Buddhi, Cintāmaṇi jewel at heart. First manifested in Śaṅkara’s heart, he is asked who he is and whether the supreme Brahman lord attained through peace-yoga.

Vakratunda says he is earlier boon-giving Gaṇeśa, forgotten by his own māyā; removes Śiva’s delusion-net and restores memory, then vanishes before hymn. Śiva’s renewed meditation fails to see him; all five compare similar experiences, abandon pride and jointly hymn Vakratunda’s form, māyā and transcendence, asking appearance. He manifests before them, raises prostrate gods, promises hymn readers honor, desired ends and final sāyujya. He warns no pride: they are dependent fractional manifestations created for play, and offers secret knowledge to remove delusion and make them like him.

Five deities request knowledge. Gaṇeśa describes fourfold deha as tvam-pada and fourfold so’ham/dehī as tat-pada; union as asi-pada with self-arising distinction, Sāṃkhya as self-bliss/other-arising, Svānanda beyond both as nondifference/union. He maps five forms: Śakti as asat; Sun as immortal/self support; Viṣṇu as Śakti/Sun delight; Śiva as fourth neti beyond three; their nondifference Svānanda. Brahmā is māyā reflection of five, creating all as Prapitāmaha. Terms retain source’s doctrinal vocabulary, not imported school equivalences.

Gaṇeśa contrasts ayoga beyond Svānanda with no entry/vision and self-experienced vision in Svānanda; yoga beyond saṃyoga/ayoga gives complete peace through mental-activity restraint. Five mental grounds are kṣipta,mūḍha,vikṣipta,ekāgra,nirodhaka, with Cintāmaṇi there; restraining them attains him as peace in heart. Buddhi is mind, Siddhi delusion, their lord plays through Brahman distinctions. Give up worry/pride in Gaṇeśa-identity samādhi to become his form without delusion. He ceases, gods abandon difference and instantly gain peace. Śiva calls the teaching21 verses; faithful reading/hearing gives Brahman likeness, worldly enjoyment then yoga, and others’ sins vanish by sight of such a person.

Gods ask how guṇa-forms are Brahman. Gaṇeśa says they are Brahman in own states, guṇa in distinction, created for play. Reflection gives fivefoldness; māyā differentiates Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Śiva as rajas/sattva/tamas, Sun as their ahaṃkāra and Śakti as delusion to accomplish three guṇas. He is here an aṃśa Vakratunda, Bindu-Brahman expressing distinction, with fourth Guṇapa/Buddhi right and five-deity play/Siddhi left. Devotees’ crooked obstacles are destroyed with trunk, explaining Vakratunda name.

Gaṇeśa explains Bindu-form supports gods’ acts/play; forgetting him brings māyā-delusion, so constant inward remembrance and first worship in divine/ancestral rites bring siddhi. He vanishes. Śiva tells Pārvatī this is his own heart meditation, that Brahmā creates, Viṣṇu preserves through manifestations at Gaṇeśa’s order, he destroys, she gives delight and Sun drives actions by time. Her Himācala-daughter birth caused forgotten knowledge; she must recover it and see heart Gaṇeśa as Mahāmāyā.

Śiva lists eight Gaṇarāja avatāras and Brahman correspondences: Vakratunda tvam; Ekadanta tat; Mahodara asi; Gajānana Sāṃkhya; Lambodara Brahman in Śakti; Vikaṭa sat/Sun; Vighnarāja sama/Viṣṇu; Dhūmravarṇa unmanifest neti/Śambhu. They are kalā forms governing eight Brahmans, supported by self-experienced Brahman; ayoga has no play, Svānanda does; full yoga transcends both. Śiva calls Gaṇeśa family deity, daily worships Cintāmaṇi/Vināyaka as light of five mental activities and shows jeweled elephant-faced household image and secluded meditation place to astonished Pārvatī.

Pārvatī asks how universal deluding Śakti became wife of partial/tamasic Śiva. He recounts seeing her power in five-deity rivalry; after Gaṇeśa instruction he propitiated her100 years. She appeared, invited boon, accepted hymn and request to be his wife, granted and vanished. Her left limb emitted Lakṣmī beloved of Nārāyaṇa, right Sāvitrī beloved of Brahmā, heart Saṃjñā wife of Sun. Śiva urges recovered Gaṇeśa yoga; Pārvatī privately practices, gains peace quickly through former impressions and returns to him. Mudgala tells Dakṣa wholehearted Gaṇeśa worship will remove obstacles/grief and make him honored yoga lord.

Śaunaka asks further Gaṇeśa accounts. Sūta resumes Dakṣa asking Mudgala why Brahman-formed Gaṇeśa incarnates and for the eight forms’ stories. Dakṣa praises sages who purify by sight, touch and speech. Mudgala praises patient, equal-minded and helpful questioners, contrasts sinners/nāstikas/dāmbhikas lacking desire for sacred narrative, and first offers his own earlier experience before the avatāra accounts.

Mudgala recounts śiloñcha gleaning and Dvādaśī fast-breaking after a fortnight, gathering a droṇa of food and performing five yajñas. Gods fear his tapas seeks their Indra/Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Śiva offices and send angry Durvāsas to test him. At fast-breaking the sage arrives naked, like a madman, asks alms and is not recognized. Mudgala gives all food; Durvāsas eats the droṇa, smears leftovers on his body and leaves. Mudgala rejoices in feeding the guest and continues fasting. The same guest consumes all food at six fast-breakings; after three months of fasting Mudgala remains unmoved, attributed to prior merit.

Pleased with pure-hearted tapas, Durvāsas reveals his yoga form and declares Mudgala pure, entitled to enjoy the conquered, imperishable heavenly worlds; he returns to his own hermitage. At once a heavenly vimāna arrives. Its ornamented messenger descends and receives Mudgala’s hospitality, says Indra with Bṛhaspati has sent him and awaits Mudgala, and invites him aboard to heavenly enjoyments.

Before accepting, Mudgala asks heavenly virtues and defects. The messenger distinguishes earthly karma-ground from heavenly enjoyment-ground: desired pleasures, youth, no fatigue/sweat/heat/cold, apsaras and desired-form movement, with enjoyment proportionate to prior karma. He admits three defects: no fresh karmic fruit there and worry about expiry; familiar gods/friends expel one without affection when merit is consumed, creating fear of falling; and envy/heart-torment on seeing those with greater merit enjoying more. Despite those defects he again invites Mudgala.

Mudgala asks for a defect-free world. Messenger says desireless karma gains Brahmaloka, Vaikuṇṭha, Śiva/Solar/Śakti worlds, yet they too have defects; Brahman-state alone is faultless and attained on earth, the karma-ground, with dharma/artha/kāma/mokṣa. Mudgala rejects heaven’s heart-torment and fall, choosing Brahman. Messenger calls him unfortunate, ignorant and foolish for refusing what tapas/yajña/dāna earns. Mudgala answers bodily heaven cannot liberate a body-bound person; asks him to convey salutation and refusal to Indra with Bṛhaspati, bows, enters his fire-hall. Messenger returns as he came.

Considering the diverse Vedic descriptions of Brahman and uncertain practice, Mudgala decides to approach Aṅgiras, expert in word-Brahman and highest Brahman, his lineage’s root ancestor. He enters the peaceful hermitage: no heat/cold, anger/desire/envy, drought/excess rain, premature death, planetary harm or rākṣasa fear; Vedic pupils and agnihotras, flowering trees, bird-filled lakes and normally hostile animals coexist without enmity. Aṅgiras sits radiant on kuśa with yogins, siddhas, sages and pupils learning Brahmavidyā. Mudgala bows and identifies himself as of Aṅgiras’s gotra.

Aṅgiras addresses Mudgala affectionately as vatsa/tāta/suta, praises his tapas and lineage honor, seats him close, and later asks his purpose. Mudgala asks the sure path to defect-free Brahman, avoiding bodily pleasures. Aṅgiras praises the future Purāṇa teacher and mantra-maker, says Vedas offer diverse Brahman descriptions successively for attainment, and begins the explanation. Affectionate son address is not treated as evidence of an immediate biological father.

Aṅgiras maps anna/prāṇa/manas/vijñāna/ānanda Brahman to their kośas; caitanya to mahākāraṇa, bindu to knowledge-body, cit to so’ham, bodha to self-utthāna, Sāṃkhya to videha, karma/jñāna to their natures, sama to delight, avyakta/sahaja to neti, Śakti to asat, Sun to self, Viṣṇu to both, Śiva to nirmoha, Svānanda to saṃyoga and nirvṛtti to ayoga. All descriptions are true in their settings, but qualifications such as self/cit delimit them. Brahman as Brahman is gained through yoga; karma/jñāna is churned toward it. Brahmaṇaspati is Brahman of Brahmans; external/internal groups, such as kinds of food, are gaṇas; Gaṇeśa is their lord. His avatāra bodies are designated knowledge etc. Brahmans; worship him for Brahman-state.

Mudgala requests avatāra greatness to worship successively for Brahman-state. Aṅgiras says Gaṇeśa’s avatāras are infinite, beyond his telling even in hundreds of years, then lists eight principal forms: Vakratunda/deha-Brahman/Matṣara/lion; Ekadanta/dehī-Brahman/Mada/mouse; Mahodara/jñāna-Brahman/Moha/mouse; Gajānana/Sāṃkhya siddhi/Loma (digital spelling)/mouse; Lambodara/Śakti-Brahman/Krodha/mouse; Vikaṭa/Solar-Brahman/Kāma/peacock; Vighnarāja/Viṣṇu-Brahman/Mamatā/Śeṣa; Dhūmravarṇa/Śiva-nature/Abhimāna/mouse. They give their respective Brahmans by worship. Destroyer/enemy words are attributed list-descriptions, not newly read battles or death outcomes.

Aṅgiras says the eight obstacle-removing forms merge in Svānanda worship, māyā also merges, and saṃyoga gives silence-samādhi. Ayoga Gaṇarāja worship ends māyā-distinction and gives supreme nirvṛtti. Yoga Gaṇeśa/Brahmaṇaspati is the peace of all forms of peace, with no higher Brahman; he urges wholehearted worship. These are doctrinal instructions, not claims of a new bodily battle.

Aṅgiras recounts complete Gaṇeśa tapas and a desired boon granted through pleased devotion: his lineage will have Gaṇeśa devotees, especially Mudgala, an unmatched past/future sovereign devotee. Beings will be uplifted by Mudgala’s bow, touch, speech, sight and wind-contact. After granting, Gaṇeśa vanished. Aṅgiras identifies the present Mudgala as this ornament of his lineage. Exact initial requested words are not separately quoted in this recollection.

Aṅgiras predicts Mudgala’s great Gaṇapatya yoga, ritually teaches the one-syllable great mantra and sends him to a forest for Gaṇeśa’s vision. Mudgala bows, leaves and performs complete exclusive tapas by that mantra’s full procedure. After1000 divine years Gaṇeśa appears: mouse-mounted, four arms, Siddhi/Buddhi, Pramoda/Āmoda entourage, elephant face, large belly, one tusk, three eyes, four weapons, Cintāmaṇi jewel at heart. Pleased by the one-syllable rite he offers a desired boon. Mudgala worships/prostrates, weeps with joy, says birth, age, knowledge, tapas, tīrthas and lineage are fulfilled by sight and even earth/trees/animals fortunate, then begins a hymn.

Śaunaka asks how Mudgala hymned Gaṇeśa; Sūta repeats it. Mudgala admits the Vedas, Brahmā and yogins cannot adequately hymn him, but Gaṇeśa’s sight/grace gives the power to praise. He salutes the supreme beyond Vedas, māyā-maker, deluder of māyā-makers, without beginning/middle/end, praised by Purāṇas and Śiva/gods.

Mudgala hymns Gaṇeśa through earth/water/light/wind, waking-gross/rajas, dreaming-subtle, causal-sleep/equanimity, caitanya/Guṇeśa/nāda/time, bindu/Vakra/deha and cit/so’ham/dehī, Ekadanta enemy of Mada, knowledge/Sāṃkhya, self-experienced silence-samādhi, Śakti/asat, Sun/sat/immortality, Viṣṇu/sama, Śambhu/neti/Dhūmravarṇa, union of four, karma/jñāna/sama/sahaja, Heramba, ayoga/nirvṛtti/yoga-peace/Jyeṣṭharāja, Brahmā creation/rajas, Viṣṇu preservation/sattva, destruction/tamas/Kailāsa/Lambodara, Sun/time/action, Śakti/delusion, Moon/nourishment/nectar/stars, Kāma/Kāmāri, praised by Hari/Indra, Śuka sages and Jaleśa/Indra/Śeṣa. Paired qualified and unqualified salutations remain hymn theology, not literal mutually contradictory incarnational biographies.

The hymn salutes Gaṇeśa as Kāśyapa, Kāpila, Vareṇya’s son, Pārāśara, Śambhu’s son, Pārśva’s child and Mādhava’s woman’s son, then universal mother/father/son/self. These are source-listed hymn designations; no birth episode or exclusive biological genealogy is narrated here. Exact Kāśyapa/Kāpila/Pārāśara contextual identities are not merged with remembered narratives.

Hymn describes noose, tusk and sṛṇi/goad, grants sons/grandsons/kingdom, enjoyment/liberation, infinite powers and names Mayūreśa/Yogeśa/Māyeśa; supports gods and all selves. It maps deha to tvam, trunk to tat, united body to asi, with Siddhi/māyā left and Buddhi right, and a neither-male-nor-female asi nature. These are explicit hymn correspondences rather than a separately narrated battle equipment change.

Hymn says hearing the three-syllable Gaṇeśa name gives joy, and those uttering it once have no birth/death. Worshippers become Brahman and give Brahman by contact, honored by Indra/gods as Gaṇeśa-formed. These are hymn efficacy claims, not independently narrated outcomes.

After the hymn Mudgala goes silent, falls prostrate and holds Gaṇeśa’s feet. Gaṇeśa raises and embraces him, names it Stotrottama, and grants its praising user enjoyment/liberation, firm devotion, freedom from distress/disease, progeny, wealth and grain. Reading21 times for21 days ends māraṇa/uccāṭana etc.; prison afflictions also end and wished ends are attained. He asks Mudgala to request boons, saying none equals his understanding/devotion and he is always under Mudgala’s control.
